solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Middle East money beginning to transform old part of Venice

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the rial is the currency of Iran, Oman and Yemen

explanation.surface: A currency change is somehow turning a historic corner of Venice into something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transform' looks like an instruction to rearrange letters, but 'beginning to' takes just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous district and bridge over the Grand Canal, an old commercial quarter of that city.

clue.text: Currency Mr Benn used touring India and Italy?

indicators.note: things used and taken touring get knocked about and moved around, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Mr Benn is a British children's cartoon character who travels to far-off places in costume
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A cartoon traveller needs to know which money to take on a trip around India and Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: RENMINBI is the official currency of China. The question mark admits the surface is fanciful: Mr Benn went on magical adventures, not package tours.
explanation.definitionFit: The renminbi is the money issued by the People's Bank of China, whose unit is the yuan.

clue.text: Likely to forget morning, since drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who has been drinking may well not remember the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs drinking and forgetting naturally, hiding that 'since' is only letters to be scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesic person suffers memory loss, so is prone to failing to recall things.

clue.text: No fool getting upset, cross

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: a git is a British insult for a stupid person

explanation.surface: Someone who is no fool gets upset and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but here it is a noun: a hybrid animal. A tigon is the offspring of a male tiger and a lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is a hybrid bred from two different big cat species, and a hybrid is called a cross.

clue.text: Like I have underwear trapped, likely to cause chafing

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside something else

blocks.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

explanation.surface: Someone complains their underwear has got caught up and is rubbing them sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' hides a two-letter word, and the trapped underwear sits after its first letter, not neatly between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive scrapes or rubs roughly against a surface, wearing it away, as a chafe does to skin.

clue.text: Theatrical performer allowed daughter, 18, to go outside

indicators.note: the other word goes on the outside, wrapping around the pair

blocks.note: 18 down is ACROBAT, and an acrobat is a balancer

explanation.surface: A performer lets their daughter, now 18, go out on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' is not an age but a cross-reference to 18 down, ACROBAT, which must then be swapped for a synonym before it goes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet dancer appears on stage in productions such as Swan Lake, so is a performer in the theatre.

clue.text: Sound equipment provided one fuller surrounds

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides

explanation.surface: Audio gear is supplied, and someone called a fuller works around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuller' looks like a person (someone who fulls cloth) but is the comparative adjective, AMPLER.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier boosts audio signals for speakers, a standard piece of hi-fi or stage kit.

clue.text: Record label turned against plugging Lennon song

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so read the letters backwards
a plug fills a hole, so this goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: EMI is a British record company
agin is a dialect form of against

explanation.surface: A record label has turned against promoting a Lennon song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugging' reads as promoting a record, the music-industry sense, but works as filling a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagine is John Lennon's best-known solo single, released in 1971.

clue.text: Bring up former philosopher

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: Revive the ideas of a thinker from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' suggests raising a topic or a child; here it is digging something up from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a buried body out of the earth, literally lifting it up.

clue.text: Minority backing Greg anonymously gathers

indicators.note: a phrase that gathers something holds it within its run of letters
going backwards means the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: read backwards within these two words

explanation.surface: A minority group is quietly supporting someone named Greg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' looks political, but it means being under age: NONAGE runs backwards through gREG ANONymously.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the legal period of youth before adulthood, also called minority in law.

clue.text: Careless hit & run?

blocks.note: a slap is a hit with an open hand
a dash is a quick run

explanation.surface: A reckless hit-and-run driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand splits 'hit-and-run' into two separate actions, joined just as & joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hasty and sloppy, done without proper attention to detail.

clue.text: Wasting extra seconds in possession infuriates sports team

indicators.note: something wasted is spoilt and ruined, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: anagram fodder: EXTRA plus S for seconds

explanation.surface: Keeping the ball to run down the clock enrages the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In possession' is surface dressing for the football scene of time-wasting; the wordplay needs only the jumbled EXTRA S and ANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texas Rangers are a Major League Baseball club based near Dallas.

clue.text: False 9 cries foul

indicators.note: something foul is bad or corrupted, so the letters come out wrong

blocks.note: the number written out, not a cross-reference

explanation.surface: A false number nine, a footballer, shouts that there has been a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9 across, but it is just the word NINE. A 'false nine' is also a football position, which explains the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person does not mean what they say, so their words are fake.

clue.text: Papers I am taking on over non-standard language

indicators.note: to take something on is to take it aboard, so it goes inside

blocks.note: O is an over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Documents of mine are being revised for language that breaks the usual rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' as O comes from cricket scoring; 'I am' must be contracted before it takes the O in.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression whose meaning cannot be worked out from its words, a departure from literal usage.

clue.text: One issuing orders to support Spanish car buyer?

blocks.note: SEAT is a Spanish car maker
the person who buys a car is taken to be its driver, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone bossing people around to promote sales of a Spanish car.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose step from car buyer to driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A backseat driver is a passenger who keeps giving unwanted instructions to whoever is at the wheel.

clue.text: Waitrose ad I cut out exchangeable for soft drink

indicators.note: something cut out is removed, so those letters are dropped
exchangeable things can be swapped around, so the letters trade places

explanation.surface: A shopper cuts a Waitrose coupon out, one that can be exchanged for a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Waitrose is a British supermarket chain. Remove I from WAITROSE AD and the remaining nine letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is fizzy carbonated water, a non-alcoholic mixer or beverage.

clue.text: Don (Republican) — following enticement — receiving shock therapy

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this letter is placed at the end
to receive something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A Republican named Don, having been lured in, undergoes shock treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a man's name, but it is the British term for a university teacher. LURE plus R takes in ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge a don is a university teacher, who gives lectures to students.

clue.text: High-ranking official coach from Australia eating yellow fruit

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: Ange Postecoglou, the Australian football manager
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A senior official and an Australian coach snack on some yellow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow fruit' reads as one phrase, but 'yellow' is OR, eaten by the MANDARIN ANGE pair at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin orange is a small citrus of the tangerine family, eaten as a dessert or snack.

clue.text: Adult Balkan national swallows a bit of brandy in tumbler

indicators.note: a small bit of a word is one letter, here its first
whatever is swallowed goes inside

blocks.note: A is the film rating for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up from the Balkans takes a sip of brandy from a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbler' suggests a drinking glass, fitting the brandy, but it is a gymnast who tumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs somersaults and flips, and people doing such gymnastics are called tumblers.

clue.text: Support Leon who wrote Japanese drama — gripping!

indicators.note: to grip is to hold, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: Leon Uris, the American novelist who wrote Exodus

explanation.surface: Get behind a gripping Japanese play written by someone called Leon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' looks like praise for the drama, but it is the instruction for NOH to hold URIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed and sustain, giving the backing something needs to grow.

clue.text: English meet up after initially showing respect

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter counts
in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom back to the top

blocks.note: taken as written, to be turned

explanation.surface: The English get together after first paying their respects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the turned MEET behind S, with E in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration felt for someone, the same as holding them in respect.

clue.text: Second husband starts to regret eloping with a harridan

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of these two words
W is an abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A second husband starts to regret running off with a nagging woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word before 'a harridan' contributes letters, making the surface read as one story.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered, scolding woman, as in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Inevitably, Muses tend to stray

indicators.note: straying means wandering from the proper path, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: The goddesses of inspiration will always drift away sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDS MUST is short for the proverb 'needs must when the devil drives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs must is said when circumstances force an unavoidable course, so it means necessarily, without choice.

clue.text: Fry small shrimp out of river

indicators.note: taking something out of a word leaves it without those letters

blocks.note: a prawn is a kind of shrimp
standard abbreviation for river, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: fry a little shrimp taken fresh from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' reads as a cooking verb, but it is a noun: young fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry are newly hatched fish, and spawn is the eggs and young produced by fish.

clue.text: Make resentful compiler put back beer

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so read it backwards

blocks.note: the setter, who compiled the puzzle, refers to themself as me
bitter is a type of British ale

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter downed a beer, which left them feeling sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as drinking a pint, the pub sense, but it turns ME round.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to fill them with bitterness and grievance, the feelings of a resentful person.

clue.text: Luxury vehicle crossing road

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one piece stretches over the other

blocks.note: via is Latin for road, as in Via Appia

explanation.surface: A luxury car drives across a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Luxury vehicle' reads as one phrase, but 'Luxury' alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar, salted sturgeon roe, is an expensive delicacy used as a byword for extravagance.

clue.text: ITV3 regularly cut out during service — insomniacs depend on it!

indicators.note: cutting out at regular intervals keeps every other letter
during means within, so this goes inside

blocks.note: read as ITVTHREE, the even letters

explanation.surface: The TV channel ITV3 keeps dropping out mid-broadcast, which at least helps the sleepless nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV3 is a British TV channel; the 3 must be spelt out as THREE before every other letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, which people struggling to sleep rely on nightly.

clue.text: Clean the rioja bottling plant partially

indicators.note: to bottle is to enclose, so the words hold the letters within

blocks.note: spans the end of one word, the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Tidy up the wine-bottling plant a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory, but it is a flowering plant, and 'partially' makes the definition a part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a stamen, a component of a flower.
